questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Under the principle of well-formed conscience, a nurse facing an ethical question must first:
questions.rationale: Inform oneself fully of facts and norms, form a morally certain judgment, act on it and accept responsibility.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Principle of well-formed conscience (PDF p. 154)
questions.quote: Informed themselves as fully as practically possible about the facts and the ethical norms

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse repeatedly cannot give the care her conscience demands because of heavy workload, and feels guilty. This is:
questions.rationale: Stress of conscience arises from repeated situations that trouble the conscience and is linked to burnout.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Conscience formation (PDF p. 154)
questions.quote: Stress of conscience is that type of stress that can arise for nurses when they repeatedly experience stressful situations that trouble their conscience.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A patient sees sin in every small act even when there is none. This type of conscience is:
questions.rationale: A scrupulous conscience judges sin to be present when there is none.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Qualities of conscience (PDF p. 155)
questions.quote: Scrupulous tends to judge sin to be present when there is none.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which type of conscience is considered the worst because it has no sensitivity to wrongdoing?
questions.rationale: A callous conscience is the worst type, with no sensitivity to sin.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Qualities of conscience (PDF p. 155)
questions.quote: Callous worst type — no sensitivity to sin.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A person who feels it is wrong to act and also wrong not to act has a(n):
questions.rationale: Perplexed: wrong if you do, wrong if you don't.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Degree of certitude (PDF p. 155)
questions.quote: Perplexed wrong if you d01ft do; wrong if you did.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse sees a moral problem but is unsure what the right action is. This is:
questions.rationale: Moral uncertainty: the nurse identifies a moral problem but is unsure of the morally correct action.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Moral distress (PDF p. 156)
questions.quote: moral uncertainty which occur when the nurse identifies a moral problem but is unsure of the morally correct action

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse is angered when a colleague performs an act she believes is immoral. This is:
questions.rationale: Moral outrage occurs when someone else in the setting performs an act the nurse believes to be immoral.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Moral distress (PDF p. 156)
questions.quote: Occurs when someone else in the health care setting performs an act the nurse believes to be immoral.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse refuses to help a colleague and criticizes her work without reason. Nurse managers classify this as:
questions.rationale: Lack of collegial behavior includes denying help, unjust criticism and not trusting colleagues' work.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Ethical problems of nurse managers (PDF p. 157)
questions.quote: criticizing colleagues without good reason, denying help to a colleague

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Value-based health care measures value as:
questions.rationale: Value is the improvement in patient outcomes relative to the cost; cost-cutting alone is not value.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Meaning and service value of care (PDF p. 158)
questions.quote: The value that underlies the implementation Of medical care can be measured by the improvement of patients' outcomes for the cost

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A standard day-by-day plan of treatment and nursing care for common dengue cases is a:
questions.rationale: Clinical pathways document a planned multidisciplinary approach for common problems to achieve cost-effective care.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Allocation of resources (PDF p. 159)
questions.quote: a clinical pathway where the day to day list of medical treatment, diagnostic procedures, laboratory work-ups and nursing care needed are placed

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In value-based care, a patient's ability to live normally while getting care is called:
questions.rationale: Outcomes: capability (doing what defines them), comfort (relief of suffering), calm (living normally during care).
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Value-based health care (PDF p. 159)
questions.quote: Calm is the ability to live normally while getting care.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the UHC Act, who finances individual-based health services?
questions.rationale: DOH and LGUs handle population-based services; PhilHealth finances individual-based services.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Issues on access to care (PDF p. 160)
questions.quote: PhilHealth will be responsible for financing individual-based health services

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the UHC Act, how long must health scholarship graduates render return service?
questions.rationale: Scholars render at least three years of compensated return service under DOH supervision, with incentives for 2 more years.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Issues on access to care (PDF p. 160)
questions.quote: graduates will be required by law to render at least three years of return service with compensation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the UHC Act, health workers are prioritized for deployment to:
questions.rationale: The national health workforce support system prioritizes deployment to Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Issues on access to care (PDF p. 160)
questions.quote: prioritizing deployment in the Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which agency implements the Data Privacy Act?
questions.rationale: The National Privacy Commission is the independent body that administers and implements the DPA.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Data Privacy Act (PDF p. 164)
questions.quote: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is the country's privacy watchdog

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A hospital posts how it collects and uses patient data. Does this posting equal patient consent?
questions.rationale: A privacy notice informs; consent is the data subject's own indication of will to the processing.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Privacy notice (PDF p. 165)
questions.quote: availability and accessibility ofa privacy notice is not equivalent to obtaining consent of a data subject

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Access to patients' health data should be granted on what basis?
questions.rationale: Only health team members needing the data for their tasks get minimum essential access.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Collecting and accessing data (PDF p. 166)
questions.quote: Access to health data must be granted solely on a "need-to-know" basis

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: During an outbreak, a barangay official wants to post the names of infected patients. The nurse should explain that:
questions.rationale: Contact tracing does not require public disclosure; unbridled disclosure has caused assault, harassment and discrimination.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Data privacy and COVID-19 (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: Contact tracing does not require public disclosure of identities of COVID-19 patients.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which three principles govern data sharing under the Data Privacy Act?
questions.rationale: The general data privacy principles are transparency, legitimate purpose and proportionality.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Sharing COVID-19 patient data (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Building data protection into a contact-tracing app from the start is called:
questions.rationale: Privacy by design makes protection of data subjects' rights integral to the system, not an add-on.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 7 Contact tracing (PDF p. 167)
questions.quote: This is called privacy by-design.
